chapter_theme: Renunciation (துறவு): Siva, himself a renouncer who lives in the burning ground and eats alms, cuts the births of those who renounce and becomes their light. The renouncer refuses the senses' claims for the tapas of reaching his feet, keeps to the path whose thorns hurt only those who stray, and, in a run of riddling images, turns the body's energies inward.
structure_note: Plain verses on Siva and the renouncer (1614 to 1618, 1620, 1622) alternate with symbolic ones whose sense is not fixed: the ploughman (1619), the five-hooded serpent (1621) and the nine gates (1623).

1614.reading: To those who, never forgetting, daily speak of the radiant Lord who saw the tapas of renouncing free of death, birth and the two deeds, the Lord of the immortals shows the abode of dharma.
1614.nuance: இருமை, the two, is usually the two kinds of deed, good and bad, though it can mean this world and the next. அறப்பதி may be the abode of dharma or Siva's realm as dharma's seat. The verse joins renunciation to unforgetting speech of the Lord rather than to bodily austerity.

1615.reading: The soul that is born and dies again through much folly, forgetting, finds that once it has renounced, at the ripe time for joining Siva's grace, its many darknesses vanish and grace becomes its blazing light.
1615.nuance: சேர்பருவம், the season of joining, is traditionally the soul's ripeness for grace, when its malas are mature. The verse makes renunciation the soul's part and the light grace's, without saying which comes first.

1616.reading: The righteous one, unborn, with no one of his own, dwells in the burning ground and eats alms; see, he too is a renouncer, the mad one who cuts off the births of those who renounce.
1616.nuance: காட்டகம் is the burning ground or the wild; பிச்சை and பித்தன் are Siva's familiar epithets as beggar and madman. The verse makes Siva the model renouncer, so the renouncer imitates the Lord rather than merely obeying him.

1617.reading: He made the path and made the thorn; if you slip from the path the thorn pierces, but for those who can walk without slipping, the path's thorns do not pierce.
1617.nuance: நெருஞ்சில் is the caltrop, a low creeper with spiked burrs that lame the barefoot walker beside a path. The plain reading is that suffering comes from straying, not from the path itself; the verse does not say whether the Lord sends the thorn as punishment or merely set it there.

1618.reading: The five came demanding ruin and their dues and closed in on me; I owe them nothing, for mine is the resolve of tapas that reaches the holy feet of the lord whose mount is the dancing bull.
1618.nuance: The image is of creditors or tax-collectors: கடமை is a due or levy, and நான் கடவேன் அலேன் 'I am not a debtor'. The five (ஐவர்) are traditionally the five senses, which the verse does not name.

1619.reading: The ploughman ploughed and the sky gave rain; a blue lily bloomed in his furrows, and saying it was like the eyes of the ploughwomen, the ploughman gave up ploughing.
1619.nuance: A riddle with no key in the verse. Read symbolically, the ploughman is the seeker, the ploughing his discipline, the rain grace and the lily the vision that makes further effort needless. Read plainly, he is distracted by a reminder of women's eyes and abandons his work. Its place in a chapter on renunciation favours the first, but both stand.

1620.reading: For those who renounce what is above, the Lord is a shining light; for those who renounce the day set by Death, he is a friend without desire; for those who renounce darkness, he stands as the one with an eye in his forehead; only those who renounce the earth can reach his state.
1620.nuance: The verse grades renunciations by what is given up (heaven, death's day, darkness, the earth) and pairs each with an aspect of Siva. மேல் and கார் are not fixed: மேல் may be the heavens, கார் dark ignorance or the rain cloud. The climax puts giving up the earth highest.

1621.reading: There is one serpent with five hoods, settled and filling the anthill of enjoyment; when its two bodies stop spreading their hoods and dancing and it makes a single hood, the body becomes its proper dwelling.
1621.nuance: The serpent is traditionally the soul with its five senses as hoods, living in the anthill of the body; the 'two bodies' (ஆகம் இரண்டு) may be the gross and subtle bodies, or the two breaths. A yogic reading takes the serpent as kundalini. நாலது in line 1 is unclear. Either way the image is of many hoods drawn into one.

1622.reading: The primal Lord, the source of the way of those who have left all, is not so easy that one can stand and say 'this is he'; Siva's feet become many, many souls, and we do not know the way his goodness comes.
1622.nuance: அகன்றார் is those who have gone away, the renouncers. சிவன் தாள் பலபல சீவனும் ஆகும் is hard: it may mean that Siva's feet are present in many souls, or that many souls reach them. நயன், goodness or grace, is left unexplained, which is the verse's point.

1623.reading: The nine gateways opened their channels and something was caught in the wallet of the one with lily-like tresses; the helmsman climbed the neem tree and looked: this is how it flowers in the temple, climbing the mast on the roof.
1623.nuance: Only the nine gates are clear: the nine openings of the body. ஆம்பல் குழலி (one whose tresses are like the water-lily, or a pipe), கஞ்சுளி (a mendicant's bag), the helmsman (மீகாமன்) on the neem, and the mast climbing to the temple are traditionally read as the breath or the yogi's awareness rising to the crown of the head, but the verse gives no key.

links.note: Both set a light against darkness in the soul. The Naladiyar's lamp is a person's own tapas, which drives out sin until its oil runs out; Tirumular's light is Siva's grace that comes to the renounced soul at its ripe time.
Both put the full renouncer above the heavens: the Kural says he who cuts 'I' and 'mine' enters a world higher than the gods', Tirumular that only he who renounces the earth reaches the Lord's state.

source_issues: 1623 is obscure throughout (ஆம்பற் குழலியின் கஞ்சுளி, வேம்பேறி, கூம்பேறி) and may be corrupt.
1621 line 1 (படம்ஐந்து நாலது) is unclear; நாலது may be a corruption.
